concepts.def: IB DP Geography HL students study three optional themes chosen from a list including freshwater, oceans, extreme environments, geophysical hazards, tourism, food and health, and urban environments.
The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries; an open system with inputs, stores, flows and outputs, central to the freshwater theme.
In the geophysical hazards theme, risk is the chance of harm, depending on the hazard event, people's exposure, their vulnerability and capacity to cope.
The maximum number of visitors a destination can support without unacceptable environmental damage or a declining visitor experience; key in the tourism theme.
The rising share of a population living in towns and cities; the urban environments theme examines its causes, megacities and management responses.
Cold high-altitude and hot arid regions with low population density, where harsh conditions and fragile ecosystems limit human activity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographic Themes (Three from the SL list) — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographic Themes (Three from the SL list) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographic Themes (Three from the SL list).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the IB Geography optional themes?
options: Geophysical hazards
Global climate - vulnerability and resilience (core unit)
Power, places and networks (HL extension)
The internal assessment fieldwork

mcqs.q: In the freshwater theme, what is a drainage basin?
options: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries
An underground water storage tank
The deepest part of the ocean
A network of water pipes in a city

mcqs.q: Hazard risk depends on the hazard event, exposure and what else?
options: Vulnerability and capacity to cope
The Richter scale value alone
Distance from the Equator
The age of the rocks

mcqs.q: In the tourism theme, carrying capacity refers to what?
options: The maximum visitor numbers a place can support without unacceptable damage
The weight a tour bus can carry
The number of hotels in a resort
A tourist's luggage allowance

mcqs.q: Do HL geography students study all of the optional themes on the list?
options: Optional themes are only studied at Standard Level.
A disaster is any event that is reported in the news.
HL students must cover every optional theme in the syllabus.
No - HL students study three optional themes from the list, while SL students study two.

mcqs.q: Is a hazard the same thing as a disaster?
options: Discharge is measured in degrees Celsius.
A disaster is any event that is reported in the news.
No - a hazard is a potentially damaging event; it becomes a disaster only when it seriously disrupts a vulnerable community that cannot cope using its own resources.
Every earthquake or flood automatically counts as a disaster.

mcqs.q: Does a river's discharge stay the same from source to mouth?
options: No - discharge usually increases downstream as tributaries join and the area being drained grows larger.
Discharge is measured in degrees Celsius.
Optional themes are only studied at Standard Level.
Rivers are biggest and most powerful near their mountain source.
